executive_summary.headline: Meta ships its first frontier model and an open-weight flagship
executive_summary.body: Muse Wonder arrived Oct 12 through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, and Muse Spark Open followed on Oct 15 with 816B parameters that Meta says run on two Mac Studios.

executive_summary.headline: Gemini 4 Argon opens broadly at $2/$10 per million tokens
executive_summary.body: The intro price holds until Nov 30, and scientists can apply for six months of top-tier Antigravity at no charge.

executive_summary.headline: Anyone can build a personal Android app in AI Studio
executive_summary.body: Google Play dropped the developer-account requirement for personal apps in select markets including the U.S.

executive_summary.headline: Creator tools: Kling 4.0 and Krea 3
executive_summary.body: Kling 4.0 generates 30-second clips with 10 keyframes, and Krea 3 edits images in under 8 seconds at native 2K.

executive_summary.headline: AI for science gets free access programs and lab connectors
executive_summary.body: OpenAI's Rosalind Academic Plan offers up to 30 free seats for 12 months, and Waters AI Link connects LC-MS instruments to agents through MCP.

top_picks.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full
top_picks.summary: Meta released Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, in two sizes. Both are built around Active Memory and Active Focus, and were trained at a gigawatt-scale data center. Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code; Muse Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code subscribers.
top_picks.author: Meta AI Research
top_picks.pricing: TechCrunch reports $4 input / $20 output per million tokens for the API.
top_picks.competitive_context: Meta lists memory and focus as the headline features and publishes API pricing at launch.
key_takeaways: Two sizes: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full.
API access through the Meta Model API; Full is Muse Code only.
Benchmark parity claims come from Meta's model card.
Memory and focus are built into the model rather than added as tooling.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: route long-running personal-assistant tasks to a model with built-in memory and compare it to your current stack on one real workflow.

top_picks.title: Gemini 4 Argon reaches broad availability
top_picks.summary: Gemini 4 Argon is now available in the paid Gemini API, in Antigravity for Ultra, and in the Gemini app and AI Mode for Pro and Ultra subscribers. It has a 1M unified token limit and 95% off cached input. Scientists can apply for six months of top-tier Antigravity at no charge.
top_picks.author: Google
top_picks.pricing: Intro price $2 input / $10 output per million tokens, rising to $4 / $20 after Nov 30.
top_picks.competitive_context: Intro pricing undercuts the new Meta flagship for the next six weeks and bundles a free research-access program.
key_takeaways: 1M unified token limit; cached input is 95% cheaper.
Antigravity runs inside the Gemini macOS app with 40+ connected apps.
Scientists can apply for six months of top-tier Antigravity at no charge.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: use the cached-input discount to put a long reference set in context once and query it all week.

top_picks.title: Meta Muse Spark Open weights
top_picks.summary: Muse Spark Open is an 816B-parameter model with 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. Meta says it runs on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios. Weights ship under the Muse Model License, with limited commercial terms, and are hosted by Baseten, Fireworks, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together.
top_picks.author: Meta AI Research
top_picks.pricing: Free weights under the Muse Model License; hosted pricing varies by provider.
top_picks.competitive_context: At 816B parameters, the largest open-weight release of the week, with a published two-machine local setup.
key_takeaways: Runs on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios per Meta.
Weights on Hugging Face, SageMaker, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: point an existing OpenAI-compatible client at OpenRouter to test the model before deciding on local hardware.

top_picks.title: Kling 4.0 launches globally
top_picks.summary: Kling 4.0 generates up to 30 seconds of native video, accepts 15 reference assets and 10 keyframes, and adds stable motion and multimodal control. It is available now on the Kling web app, with API access to follow. Kling says it has 100M+ users.
top_picks.author: Kling AI
top_picks.pricing: Available in the Kling web app; API pricing not yet published.
top_picks.competitive_context: Raises single-generation length to 30 seconds and adds keyframe control, which narrows the gap to multi-shot editing workflows.
key_takeaways: 15 reference assets and 10 keyframes per project.
Press release distributed on GlobeNewswire on Oct 16.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: storyboard a product demo with 10 keyframes and render it as one continuous clip instead of stitching short shots.

top_picks.title: Google Play: build personal Android apps in AI Studio, no developer account
top_picks.summary: Google Play now lets people build personal Android apps in AI Studio without a developer account. The feature is rolling out in select markets, including the U.S., for users 18 and older. The same update adds Ask Play and Game Finder.
top_picks.author: Google
top_picks.pricing: No developer-account fee for personal apps; availability by market.
top_picks.competitive_context: Moves app-making from developers to anyone with a prompt, on the distribution platform that already sits on every Android phone.
key_takeaways: No developer account needed for personal apps.
Rolling out in select markets including the U.S., 18+.
Ask Play and Game Finder ship in the same update.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: build a single-purpose personal app, such as a household chore tracker, and install it on your own phone.

top_picks.title: ChatGPT Chrome extension can control open tabs
top_picks.summary: The ChatGPT Chrome extension can now act in open tabs in Work mode: sending messages, filling out forms, downloading files and organizing tabs. It works in the background without taking over the active session. It also runs in Edge, Brave and Opera.
top_picks.author: OpenAI
top_picks.pricing: Listed on the Chrome Web Store; plan requirements not stated.
top_picks.competitive_context: Brings computer-use style control into the browser people already have open, alongside the desktop app's built-in browser.
key_takeaways: Chat mode reads across open tabs; Work mode acts in them.
Tasks include forms, messages, downloads and tab grouping.
Permission prompts appear for browser history and file uploads or downloads.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand it the weekly timesheet or expense form and let it fill the fields from the tabs you already have open.

top_picks.title: OpenAI Rosalind Academic Plan for university labs
top_picks.summary: The Rosalind Academic Plan gives eligible U.S. university labs up to 30 ChatGPT Business Standard seats at $0 for 12 months. GPT-Rosalind access requires trusted-access approval and covers seven life-science areas. API access is not included.
top_picks.author: OpenAI
top_picks.pricing: $0 for 12 months for up to 30 Business Standard seats; eligibility applies.
top_picks.competitive_context: Pairs with Google's six-month scientist grant for Gemini 4 Argon: both labs are competing for research users this week.
key_takeaways: Up to 30 seats free for 12 months.
API access is not part of the plan.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: apply for both the Rosalind plan and the Antigravity grant and compare them on one literature-review task.

top_picks.title: Krea 3 image editing model
top_picks.summary: Krea 3 is an image editing model that finishes edits in under 8 seconds at native 2K and keeps products, characters and materials consistent across references. It is the default image model in the Krea app and costs compute units. Krea 3 Ultra is on Max plans and above.
top_picks.author: Krea
top_picks.pricing: App use costs compute units; API from $0.03 per 1K image (early access).
top_picks.competitive_context: Focuses on keeping products and characters consistent across edits.
key_takeaways: Edits in under 8 seconds at native 2K.
API combines up to 8 reference images and offers regional edits.
API is in early access for beta workspaces.
Krea's press kit lists Oct 12; the in-app release followed on Oct 15.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: upload one product photo and generate a full set of seasonal scenes with the item left unchanged.

sections.title: Product Hunt and Indie Launches
sections.description: Top launches of the week by Product Hunt upvotes; maker site is the primary link.

items.title: Pancake
items.summary: Pancake positions itself as the Vercel for go-to-market work, with MCP access and 40+ data providers.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: Jockey by TwelveLabs
items.summary: Jockey searches a video and photo library by person, moment or insight, and recognizes the same person across thousands of files. Available in research preview through the API and MCP on Claude.
items.author: Product Hunt
items.pricing: Free (5 GB), Plus $20/month (100 GB), Pro $100/month (500 GB).

items.title: Inferock
items.summary: Serverless inference that returns credits for failed calls and issues a receipt per call.
items.author: Product Hunt
items.pricing: Watch is free; Serve is supplier cost plus a 10% fee.

items.title: Articos MCP
items.summary: Simulated buyers react to messaging inside your agent; Articos reports 86% validated accuracy across 46 studies.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: Talanoa
items.summary: Email that reads like chat, with on-device AI.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: Harness by Autonomous
items.summary: A free, open-source command center for coding agents with 49 harnesses, including CAD and circuit design.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: OpenCode 2.0
items.summary: The open-source AI coding agent reaches version 2.0.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: ngram 2.0
items.summary: An AI video agent that creates explainers, screencasts and avatar videos.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: Inbox Zero
items.summary: An open-source AI email assistant positioned as a Superhuman alternative.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: Fina Business
items.summary: A $20/month QuickBooks alternative for founders with double-entry bookkeeping, invoices, Stripe payments and AI categorization. Supports up to 5 profiles across personal and business finances.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: Navige
items.summary: Routes agent calls to cut AI spend; the Watchtower tier is free.
items.author: Product Hunt

items.title: Retriever AI
items.summary: A free AI browser agent that finds leads, sends outreach and applies to jobs.
items.author: Product Hunt

sections.title: Frontier Models and AI for Science
sections.description: New model releases and lab-automation launches.

items.title: Reflection Beam open weights
items.summary: Beam has 501B total and 23B active parameters, a 1M-token context window and an Apache 2.0 license. It ships in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4. It is free to start on Reflection and available through Hugging Face inference providers and SageMaker JumpStart.
items.author: Reflection AI
items.pricing: Free to start on Reflection; Apache 2.0 weights.
items.competitive_context: Apache 2.0 licensing, compared with the limited commercial terms on Muse Spark Open.
key_takeaways: Hosted on Hugging Face providers and SageMaker JumpStart.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: use the NVFP4 build to test whether a 23B-active model fits your own GPU budget.

items.title: xAI Grok Voice 3.0
items.summary: Grok Voice 3.0 ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Speech Index at 86.9. The API costs $0.08 per minute, and the grok-voice-latest alias switched to the new model automatically.
items.author: xAI
items.competitive_context: Competes directly with OpenAI's GPT-Live-1.1 voice update from the same week.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: swap the voice model behind a phone-answering or tutoring demo and compare latency side by side.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt
items.summary: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B open vision-language model that NVIDIA says is 5x faster than the next-best model in its class. Bolt 74B-A9B fits in 24GB, and a 4GB Bolt E4B is due Oct 23. Models are on Hugging Face, OpenRouter and NIM.
items.author: NVIDIA
items.pricing: Open weights; hosted on OpenRouter and NIM.
items.competitive_context: Bolt targets a single 24GB GPU, with a 4GB variant to follow.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run Bolt on a 24GB card to caption and tag a personal photo or product archive.

items.title: Liquid AI d1-ultra decision model
items.summary: d1-ultra is a decision model priced at $0.042 per million input tokens. Liquid AI claims an 8-point gain on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index.
items.author: Liquid AI
items.competitive_context: A model class aimed at choosing among options rather than generating text.
key_takeaways: Priced at $0.042 per million input tokens.
+8 points on the Decision Index per Liquid AI.

items.title: Noiz Helix World real-time audio-visual world model
items.summary: Helix World generates audio and video in real time at 24 fps on a single H800. A demo is live at helixworld.org and a preview checkpoint is on Hugging Face.
items.author: Noiz
items.pricing: Demo and preview checkpoint are free.
items.competitive_context: Ships a live demo and a downloadable preview checkpoint.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
items.summary: The 1017 update scores 77.0 on DeepSWE v1.1 and 92.5 on BabyVision with tools. API pricing is unchanged, and the release adds a DeepSeek Search mention.
items.author: DeepSeek
items.competitive_context: A quality update with no price change.

items.title: Jais 3 open Arabic model family
items.summary: Jais 3 is six open Arabic models from 900M to 375B parameters with 512K context, released with Jais Speech.
items.author: IFM and Inception42
items.competitive_context: Spans small on-device models to a 375B model in one family.

items.title: Waters AI Link connects lab instruments to AI agents
items.summary: AI Link brings MCP to waters_connect software, so agents can create methods, run acquisitions and process LC-MS results without custom integration. It works with Claude and other LLMs. Waters also joined the Model Hardware Standard research program. Early access is open; general availability is planned for November.
items.author: Waters
items.competitive_context: Another instrument maker connects lab hardware to agents through an open protocol.
key_takeaways: Early access now; GA in November.
Joins the Model Hardware Standard program.

sections.title: YC and Startups
sections.description: Launch HN and Y Combinator companies shipping this week.

items.title: Agent37 (YC F26) low-cost agent sandboxes
items.summary: Agent37 hosts personal agents and sandboxes at an average of $0.37 per sandbox per month. It has a free plan, and says its default sandboxes cost under 10% of most providers. Launch HN thread has 162 points and 128 comments.
items.author: Launch HN
items.pricing: Free plan; $4.94/month for a 2 vCPU / 4 GB box.

items.title: Consus (YC F24) LLM gateway for controlled data
items.summary: Consus offers an OpenAI-compatible gateway that routes requests to ITAR and FedRAMP High infrastructure. It has completed a FedRAMP equivalency audit against 410 High controls.
items.author: Launch HN
items.pricing: From $40 per seat per month plus tokens at cost.

items.title: Neomatter (YC F26) operating system for in-house legal
items.summary: Neomatter reads legal requests from email, Slack and Salesforce, does the redlines and drafts the reply, and queues the work for a lawyer to review and send.
items.author: Y Combinator

items.title: Elorian Glimpse
items.summary: Elorian's first model, Glimpse, reasons with images rather than only describing them. It is in research preview with an API and a waitlisted chat app. The startup raised a $55M seed at a $300M valuation.
items.author: TechCrunch
items.pricing: API in research preview; chat is waitlisted.

sections.title: Consumer, Creator, and Small-Business Tools
sections.description: Apps and features for individuals, creators and small teams.

items.title: Train with Pasta
items.summary: Train with Pasta is an iPhone workout app that runs on Apple Intelligence and includes an 873-exercise library. It needs iOS 27.
items.author: Pasta

items.title: Winq
items.summary: Winq controls a Mac with gaze and winks, using on-device processing.
items.author: Winq

items.title: Tabby 2.0 with Tabby Talk
items.summary: Tabby 2.0 adds Tabby Talk, a bookkeeping agent for small businesses. Tabby reports 6,000+ small-business users and 200+ accounting firms.
items.author: Yahoo Finance

items.title: OpenAI GPT-Live-1.1, Quip and prompt-to-voice
items.summary: GPT-Live-1.1 and the Quip voice arrived in ChatGPT Voice on Oct 15. On Oct 16 prompt-to-voice opened to all API customers with 9 new GPT-Live voices, and creating a voice is free.
items.author: OpenAI

items.title: Pulse Local
items.summary: Pulse Local is a Mac budgeting app that runs its AI models on the device. Spending answers are computed from your transactions, and an optional 2.5 GB checker reads each answer twice. A money answer takes 12-14 seconds with the checker on.
items.author: Pulse Local
items.pricing: Free; optional one-time payments of $20, $40 or any amount; Sync Pass $29/year.

items.title: Apple iPhone Duo and Siri AI beta
items.summary: iPhone Duo is a foldable iPhone with a 7.58-inch inner display and the A20 Pro chip. It runs iOS 27, which brings the Siri AI beta in English. Preorders opened Oct 16 at 5 a.m. PT, with leases from $57.99 per month.
items.author: Apple
items.pricing: Leases from $57.99/month for 24 months; full retail price not stated.

items.title: Adobe and NVIDIA RTX Spark optimization
items.summary: Adobe and NVIDIA expanded their partnership with RTX Spark optimization for Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, up to 2x faster.
items.author: TV Technology

sections.title: Enterprise AI
sections.description: Platform releases; kept to a small share of the week's mix.

items.title: Microsoft Maia 300 inference chip
items.summary: Microsoft announced Maia 300, which it expects to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems. A 96-accelerator rack delivers up to 7x the token throughput of Maia 200. Production deployments begin in 2027.
items.author: Microsoft

sections.title: Funding
sections.description: Funding rounds checked against the company's own announcement.

items.title: Albert raises $55M Series B for chemistry-native AI
items.summary: Albert, a chemistry-native AI operating system for R&D, raised $55M in a Series B led by TCV. Yahoo Finance coverage reports 45x higher accuracy on scientific retrieval for its Valence model and 6x more scientist users across 44 countries.
items.author: Albert

items.title: Ramp raises $1.85B at a $60B valuation
items.summary: Ramp raised $1.85B at a $60B valuation, four months after a $750M round at $44B. Ramp reports 85,000 businesses and over $2B in annualized revenue. TechCrunch lists Dragoneer, Thrive, Founders Fund, Sands and Avenir as co-leads.
items.author: Ramp

items.title: SolidCraft open-source parametric CAD
items.summary: SolidCraft is a parametric 3D CAD application built in Rust. It runs on desktop and in the browser, and exposes an MCP server so agents can edit designs. It has 5.5k stars and an MIT or Apache-2.0 license; the project calls itself early but usable for simple parts.
items.author: GitHub

items.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein open weights
items.summary: FLUX 3 Image Klein has 5.6B parameters and open weights under the FLUX Kommunity License.
items.author: Black Forest Labs

items.title: Sphinx
items.summary: Sphinx is a free, open-source Git hook that asks you a question about your agent's diff before a push goes through. It works with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode and Pi.
items.author: Show HN

items.title: llmspeed
items.summary: llmspeed estimates tokens per second and time to first token for local models across about 30 GPUs, Macs and cloud chips. Figures come from community benchmarks, and the project is open source.
items.author: Show HN

items.title: rStation
items.summary: rStation is a research community for AI agents that discuss six open problems, including the Riemann hypothesis and the Earth-Moon problem, and publish reviewed papers. Humans can observe.
items.author: Show HN

items.title: PDF TO MP3 MCP and plugin
items.summary: PDF TO MP3 turns PDFs into audiobooks from inside Codex or Claude through an MCP server and a Codex plugin. The service is free; speech generation is billed by Google or OpenAI per use.
items.author: Show HN
items.pricing: Free service; speech generation billed per use by the provider.

items.title: StarSkirmish Bench v0.2
items.summary: StarSkirmish tests how strong a StarCraft: Brood War bot a model can write in one hour. Gemini 4 Argon placed third, statistically tied with two Claude models in the 37-39 range.
items.author: Show HN

emerging_signals.pattern: Free research access is a competitive lever
emerging_signals.evidence: Google offers six months of Antigravity for scientists and OpenAI offers 30 seats for 12 months, both announced within three days.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether Anthropic or Meta announce comparable programs.

emerging_signals.pattern: Large open weights are now designed for desktop hardware
emerging_signals.evidence: Muse Spark Open targets two Mac Studios, Bolt fits 24GB, and Beam ships NVFP4 builds.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Local inference numbers on llmspeed for these models.

emerging_signals.pattern: Agents move into the browser and lab bench
emerging_signals.evidence: ChatGPT's Chrome extension acts in tabs, and Waters AI Link lets agents run LC-MS acquisitions.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Native MCP support in more instrument and browser products.

suggested_refinements.notes: Source gaps: Product Hunt pages return 403 to direct HTTP checks, so PH product-page links were taken from the weekly leaderboard and page fetches and were not individually status-checked. Direct checks also returned 403 for the OpenAI release notes and Rosalind page, ifm.ai, the Waters investor page, the Microsoft blog and GlobeNewswire; those pages rendered real content in the fetch tool or search index. The OpenAI release notes page has no per-entry anchor. The Krea blog post URL was not found, so the model page is the primary link, and Krea's press kit (Oct 12) and in-app release (Oct 15) differ. The Black Forest Labs link is the blog index. Show HN points come from the Hacker News API; the Fina and Pulse Local maker pages are the primary links. SignWith (221 upvotes) was skipped because no maker page was resolved. EmbeddingGemma 2 (PH rank 8) was excluded because it launched Oct 6.
